context:
Source: DataFrame query parity proposal v3 (item T13). The SF=1 180.29 s figure is the probe's own 180 s alarm, so it is a lower bound. Project owner does NOT accept earlier reviewers' TPC-H claims.

CAUSE (TESTED by cProfile at SF 0.1): essentially all time is the nine groupby agg calls using lambda values.sum(min_count=1) (_python_agg_general, one Python call per group). Fix: built-in sum plus count, masking empty groups (keeps SQL all-NULL SUM is NULL). Evidence: SF 0.1 pandas Q78 14.26 s before, 0.32 s after (single runs, loaded machine); output identical to before (assert_frame_equal, values, order and dtypes); full probe at 0.1: no cell changed status, pandas total 24.0 s to 9.9 s; staged gate at 0.01 unchanged; new unit test passes on old code, fails when the mask is removed. Q78 status before/after: still divergent on both families at 0.1 (separate cause: the committed baseline note shows None vs 0.0 in an ORDER BY key; not diagnosed here). NOT done: the SF=1 completion criterion needs explicit approval for the run (about 450 s and 3.5 GB); until then the bound is only that SF=0.1 is about 44x faster. Remaining: hosted CI, maintainer merge, SF=1 run if approved, then finish.

Profile the pandas implementation (likely a non-vectorized or quadratic step), fix it, and keep results unchanged or corrected. This blocks the SF=1 oracle lane (dfparity-t18) and the pandas parallel job.
